title: Note Deduplication Triggers Redundant AI Processing
evidence: NoteService.createNote unconditionally calls serviceScope.launch { enrichNote(...) } using the ID returned from noteRepository.create, even if NoteDeduplicationManager returned an existing ID.
root_cause: The repository layer hides the distinction between an 'inserted' note and a 'retrieved duplicate' note. The service layer assumes all returned IDs require processing.
reproduction_steps: Send POST /data/notes with the same content multiple times. Observe the server re-running content analysis and overwriting the database row.

title: OpenCode CLI Network Retry Duplicates Messages
evidence: OpencodeLlmProvider.kt contains a 'while(true)' loop around client.preparePost. Exceptions thrown during stream read trigger a full retry.
root_cause: Retrying an HTTP POST to an stateful session endpoint without idempotency keys appends a duplicate message to the daemon's context window.
reproduction_steps: Initiate a chat session. Terminate the Ktor client connection mid-stream. Observe the daemon logs receiving the same prompt twice.

title: Streaming Parser Swallows Intermediate Text
evidence: In the regex logic for '</think>|<final>', any text between the closing think tag and the opening final tag is incorrectly assigned to thinkingPart instead of cleanContent.
root_cause: Incorrect array indexing and state assignment in the regex split block.
reproduction_steps: Simulate an LLM chunk containing '</think> Intermediate <final>'. The word 'Intermediate' will be invisible in the final output.

title: Database Schema Desync: Sync Queue Ignored
evidence: SUPABASE_SCHEMA.sql defines sync_queue and conflict_records, but no Kotlin backend code references them. OptimizedSyncRoutes uses direct UPSERTs.
root_cause: Schema was designed for an asynchronous queue-based sync, but the backend implementation shifted to synchronous delta-syncs.

title: Missing Cancellation Propagation to Daemon
evidence: No code exists to send an abort/cancel signal to the OpenCode HTTP server if the Ktor request is cancelled.
root_cause: Unidirectional HTTP POST assumption for streams.
reproduction_steps: Start a long-running generation. Disconnect the client. Observe the daemon continuing to use CPU.
